hook_verdict.fig1_is: A PRISMA flow diagram: 8,170 records screened down to 55 records / 54 studies / 51 independent works. This is a methods-credibility figure, not a hook.
hook_verdict.fig1_should_be: The Fig4 'two design cultures' contrast (token-native ~100 ranked gene names vs encoder-mediated 331-20,541 features compressed into 1-256 vectors with a third of steps opaque) — reframed as THE finding, not a late-paper reveal. PRISMA flow should move to supplement/methods figure, referenced but not leading.
hook_verdict.why: A general scientist opening this paper needs to see the conflict and stakes in panel one: two incompatible design philosophies are silently deciding what biological signal survives, and nobody has tested them against each other fairly. A PRISMA diagram proves rigor but answers a question ('was this review done properly?') the reader hasn't asked yet. It is evidence for peer reviewers, not a hook for anyone else. Leading with it risks the desk-reject read of 'yet another scoping review' before the actual contribution — a structural, field-wide blind spot plus a protocol to fix it — registers at all.

figure_moves.to_fig: Fig1 (demoted to small inset) / Methods appendix
figure_moves.why: Needed for rigor and reproducibility claims but is not the story; burying the hook behind it costs the paper its first impression on a general-scientist audience.

figure_moves.what: Two design cultures contrast (token-native ranks vs encoder-mediated vectors, opacity fraction)
figure_moves.why: This is explicitly named as the most arresting asset and is the entire thesis in one picture. It should be what the reader sees first, with PRISMA rigor following as support.

figure_moves.what: The 19/22 reused operations with missing-parameter reporting gap
figure_moves.why: Fig3's replication-failure point and Fig5's structural-not-incidental point are two cuts of the same underlying fact (shared vocabulary of operations, poorly reported); merging avoids making the reader learn the operation-library concept twice before reaching the payoff in Fig6.

figure_moves.what: Authors' own stated trade-off language (9/17 unchanged architecture, 9/17 prior knowledge, 7/17 concede loss; 7/16 criticise text rendering)
figure_moves.why: This belongs next to the self-assessment and comparison-bias evidence — the irony that both cultures already admit the trade-off in prose yet almost never test it or compare fairly lands much harder as one evidentiary figure than scattered across the culture-description figure.

missing_panels.what_to_show: A paired bar/strip panel per work showing (x-axis) each of the 33 token-native+encoder-mediated works, (y-axis, left) fraction of features retained vs dropped, (y-axis, right) opacity fraction, colored by culture — so the reader sees the complementary-loss pattern across the whole corpus, not just two exemplar numbers.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: Per-work tabulation already charted (median 100 genes/50-1000 range; 331-20,541 features into 1-256 vectors; 0.33 opaque steps) needs to be plotted per-work rather than only reported as medians/ranges, so readers can see variance and outliers, not just central tendency.

missing_panels.what_to_show: A 2x2 panel: (1) bar chart of dependence-testing rate by culture (22/51 overall, 4/16 encoder-mediated) with a highlighted gap; (2) win-rate chart of 28/31 cross-culture comparisons split into within-culture vs cross-culture (20/23 between-system, p=4.9e-4), annotated with baseline strength (weakest-opponent flag) and the two upsets (120B vs 8B; more single-cell text) called out as exceptions proving the rule.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: This is the evidentiary core of the whole paper's claim that comparative evidence cannot be trusted - it currently reads only as abstract text. It needs its own fully worked quantitative figure, not a supporting panel, given it is the basis for the paper's central recommendation (neutral comparison protocol).

missing_panels.what_to_show: A mock-up or schematic of the proposed 'reporting card' for input representations (the concrete deliverable promised in the abstract) — e.g., a template showing what any future paper should disclose: features kept/discarded, opacity fraction, dependence test (yes/no), baseline strength, comparison type.
missing_panels.analysis_needed: No analysis — this is a design/template figure, but it is the paper's actual proposed intervention and is currently entirely absent from the figure list. Without it, the 'application' beat of the story (what should a reviewer or builder DO differently tomorrow) has no visual anchor.

kill_list.what: Full PRISMA flow diagram detail (per-source counts across 8 databases, 5 search rounds) as a headline figure
kill_list.why: Important for methodological trust and should exist, but it is reproducibility bookkeeping, not discovery; placing it as Fig1 signals 'systematic review' genre fatigue to a general-scientist reader before the finding is visible.

kill_list.what: Fig2's full taxonomy of input-carrier families, fusion topologies, and text roles as a standalone descriptive figure
kill_list.why: This is useful field-mapping context but is purely descriptive ('the field is diverse and growing') with no tension or claim; as currently scoped it risks reading as a figure that exists because the data was collected, not because it argues anything.

kill_list.what: Fig3's operation-parameter non-reporting statistic as its own figure
kill_list.why: Overlaps substantially with Fig5's sub-chain analysis; keeping both as separate full figures forces the reader through the same 'operations are reused but poorly documented' point twice before reaching the two-cultures payoff.

arc.one_line: Two silently competing design cultures decide what biological signal a text-biology model can ever see — and nobody has compared them fairly.
The field is young (post-2023), fast-growing, and structurally diverse in how it wires text to biology.
That apparent diversity collapses into 15 recurring operation sub-chains that cleanly sort into the two cultures, with the operations' key parameters chronically unreported.
Token-native keeps gene identity as ranked names; encoder-mediated keeps magnitude in opaque compressed vectors — complementary, incomplete, and each culture already admits it.

Almost nobody tests whether their model actually depends on the biological input, and when cultures compare themselves to each other, the proposing side wins 28/31 — almost always against the rival's weakest baseline.
A neutral comparison protocol and reporting card lets any editor or reviewer demand dependence-testing and fair baselines before trusting a cross-culture win claim.

boldest_defensible_fig1: A single two-panel figure that IS the current Fig4: left panel shows a token-native cell as a ranked list of ~100 gene names (text tokens); right panel shows an encoder-mediated cell as a dense heatmap of 331-20,541 features collapsing into a 32-dim vector with ~1/3 of the pipeline shaded out as 'opaque learned module.' A single sentence under both: '51 models, two incompatible answers to what biology a language model is allowed to see — and no fair test of which is right.' This is defensible as Fig1 because it is concrete, visually self-explanatory to a general scientist with zero review-methodology background, and it states the paper's entire claim before any PRISMA scaffolding is needed; the systematic-review rigor (Fig1-original) can follow immediately as Fig2/methods proof that this contrast is representative of 51 works, not two cherry-picked examples.
